claims.text: Faults are exposed by dry runs, walkthroughs and testing; a dry run traces the code by hand on paper, a walkthrough is a guided trace with the code's author, and testing runs the code on data chosen to find faults.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language and is found when the program fails to translate; a logic error breaks the program's meaning and is found when it runs but gives the wrong result; a run-time error stops the program while it runs, on an operation the program cannot complete.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A trace table - a dry run recording each variable's value after each statement - exposes what the program actually does, so a logic error is found by comparing the traced values with the values the problem required.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Correcting an identified error means finding the statement that causes the traced wrong value, changing that statement, and re-running the test that exposed the error - and only that statement, because the error's location is what the trace established.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The testing methods form a series: dry run and walkthrough before running; white-box testing uses the code's structure to choose test data; black-box testing uses only the specification; integration testing checks separately tested modules together; stubs stand in for unfinished modules; alpha testing is in-house, beta testing is with selected users, and acceptance testing is the customer checking the requirements.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Integration testing checks that separately tested modules work together, because modules that each pass alone can still fail together at their interfaces.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A test strategy states what will be tested and how; a test plan is the concrete schedule that follows it, listing the tests, the data, the expected results and the actual results - so the plan is the strategy written down as work that can be checked off.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Test data is chosen by kind: normal data is valid data in the ordinary range; abnormal data is invalid data the program should reject; extreme data is valid data at the limits of the acceptable range; boundary data tests either side of a limit, because errors sit at the edges of ranges.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Abnormal data is chosen to be rejected - a negative age, a name of digits - because the program's response to invalid data is a behaviour worth testing.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Corrective maintenance fixes errors found in use; adaptive maintenance responds to a change in the environment or requirements around a working program; perfective maintenance improves a working program that meets its requirements - so the kind is named by why the program is being changed.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Maintenance continues for the program's whole working life, because errors surface in use, the environment around a program changes, and users see improvements they want - so a program left unchanged while the world around it moves is a program quietly becoming unusable.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Amending a program to enhance its functionality: read the existing code with a trace to learn what it does, place the change at the statement that owns the affected value, add the new functionality as new statements or modules that follow the existing style, and re-test the whole program, because a change to one value travels to every use of it.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
